45921.dm: kõrgus: 55.0 cm; laius: 88.6 cm; kõrgus: 50.8 cm; laius: 92.9 cm
45921.d: Maria Kapajeva on käsile võtnud mitte just kõige uuema, kuid visalt aktuaalsena püsiva teema naise kohast ja rollist ühiskonnas ning tema õigusest otsustada oma keha ja elu eesmärkid üle. Teema sai tervikliku kunstilise väljenduse 1920. aastal Tallinna Kunstihoone galeriis toimunud isikunäitusel „Kui maailm õhku lendab, loodan lahkuda tantsides“. Näitus äratas elavat tähelepanu, selle mõjukus võimendus samal aastal aset leidnud Poola sündmuste taustal, kus tuhanded naised astusid välja abordi keelustamise vastu.
45921.de: Maria Kapajeva has taken up a theme that is not exactly the newest but remains stubbornly topical – the place and role of women in society and their right to decide the goals of their own body and life. The theme received a comprehensive artistic expression at the solo exhibition "When the World Blows Up, I Hope to Leave Dancing" held at the Tallinn Art Hall gallery in 1920. The exhibition attracted lively attention, and its impact was amplified by the background of events taking place in Poland that same year, where thousands of women came out against the banning of abortion.

46238.d: Krista Leesi on eesti tekstiilikunstnik ja -disainer, kelle loomingut iseloomustab keele ja visuaalse kujutise nutikas kontseptuaalne ühendamine. Tuttavad objektid, pildid ning keskkonnad saavad Leesi sekkumisel uue ja teravmeelse tähenduse.
46238.de: Krista Leesi is an Estonian textile artist and designer, whose work is characterised by a clever conceptual combination of language and visual image. Familiar objects, pictures and environments acquire, through Leesi's intervention, a new and witty meaning.

46278.dm: lehe kõrgus: 110.0 cm; lehe laius: 105.0 cm
46278.d: Kadri Toom on keskendunud eksperimentaalsele kaasaegsele graafikale. Ta loob loodusmotiividest ja arhitektoonidest, antud seerias ka Buckminster Fulleri kuplite ja ajalooliste kasvuhoonete kujutistest koosnevaid müstilisi vaikusega täidetud värvilisi ruume. Kunstnik kasutab väga erinevaid tehnikaid, tsüanotüüpia, kõrgtrükk, siiditrükk, sügavtrükk, ta trükib oma plaadid ise, kõik teosed on unikaalsed, igaüht on vaid üks tõmmis.
46278.de: Kadri Toom has focused on experimental contemporary print art. From nature motifs and architectonic forms — in this series also images of Buckminster Fuller's domes and historical greenhouses — she creates mystical, silence-filled coloured spaces. The artist uses very different techniques: cyanotype, relief printing, screen printing, intaglio printing; she prints her plates herself, all works are unique, each with only one impression.

Kris Lemsalu kombineerib oma teostes portselani karusnaha, villa, tekstiili, silikooni, leidobjektid, helid ja teised materjalid isemeelse huumoriga sürrealistlikeks stseenideks, mis on niisama peadpööritavalt sümbolistlikud kui lustlikud.
Installatsioon „Vihmased päevad“ on Kris Lemsalu tõlgendus Tartus igavesse suudlusse jäätunud purskkaevust. See valmis 2024. aastal Tartu Kunstimuuseumis toimunud Lemsalu isikunäituse „DONATELLA. Elukeeris” jaoks. 
Nagu Kris Lemsalu ise hiljuti Tõnu Karjatsele antud intervjuus ütles: „Ma olen leidnud oma maailma ja oma keele ja see on erinev, sellepärast see paistabki natuke välja. Mõnele meeldib, mõnele ei, mõnd ärritab, mõnd tülgastab, inimesi on igasugu
46299.de:
In her works, Kris Lemsalu combines porcelain, fur, wool, textile, silicone, found objects, sounds and other materials with a wilful sense of humour into surrealist scenes that are as dizzyingly symbolist as they are playful.
The installation "Vihmased päevad" ["Rainy Days"] is Kris Lemsalu's interpretation of the fountain in Tartu frozen forever in a kiss. It was created in 2024 for Lemsalu's solo exhibition "DONATELLA. Elukeeris" ["DONATELLA. Whirl of Life"] held at the Tartu Art Museum. 
As Kris Lemsalu herself recently said in an interview given to Tõnu Karjatse: "I have found my own world and my own language, and it is different, that's why it stands out a little. Some people like it, some don't, some it irritates, some it disgusts, there are all kinds of people

46507.d:
Foto pärineb Cloe Jancise ja Sigrid Viiri näituselt "Mõnel reipamal päeval paned sa oma maski peegli ees liiga tugevasti ette, nii et hammustab su nahka". Näituse sünni algimpulsiks on 2020. kevadel Fotomuuseumi poolt ellukutsutud projekt „Isolatsioonidialoogid“, mille eesmärk oli jäädvustada isolatsiooniaja tunnetust ja uut tekkinud olukorda. Näituse pealkiri pärineb Maris Karjatse lühiesseest. 
 Kunstnike visuaalne kahekõne kulges üksteise ideid tõlgendades, miksides ja edasi arendades. Nende dialoog toob esile huumori ja absurdi kui ühe võimaliku kaitsemehhanismi ja väljapääsuvõimaluse mentaalsest ja füüsilisest kitsikusest isolatsiooniajal. Fotosid toetavad installatiivsed raamid.
46507.de:
The photo comes from Cloe Jancis and Sigrid Viir's exhibition "On some more energetic days you put on your mask too firmly in front of the mirror, so that it bites into your skin". The impulse for the birth of the exhibition was the project "Isolation Dialogues" initiated by the Photography Museum in spring 2020, the aim of which was to document the sense of the isolation period and the newly arisen situation. The title of the exhibition comes from a short essay by Maris Karjatse.
The artists' visual dialogue proceeded by interpreting, mixing and further developing each other's ideas. Their dialogue brings out humour and absurdity as one possible defence mechanism and way out of mental and physical hardship during the isolation period. The photographs are supported by installational frames.

47037.d: Muravskaja kes tavaliselt reageerib teravalt ühiskondlikele probleemidele, pöördub seekord vee ja valguse läbi nähtud poeetiliste abstraktsete kujutluspiltide poole. Ise on ta oma tööde kohta öelnud: „Oma töödega kutsun ka vaatajat aeglustama ja häälestama pilku ümber – astuma kõrvale lõputust uudiste- ja pildivoost, et taastada tundlikkus valguse ja aja suhtes ning märgata, kuidas kujutis sünnib siin ja praegu. See on rännak nähtava ja nähtamatu piirile, mis toob vaataja tagasi teravdatud füüsilisse kohalolusse.“
47037.de: Muravskaja, who usually reacts sharply to social problems, turns this time to poetic abstract imagery seen through water and light. She has said of her works: "With my works I also invite the viewer to slow down and re-tune their gaze – to step aside from the endless stream of news and images, in order to restore sensitivity to light and time, and to notice how the image is born here and now. It is a journey to the border between the visible and the invisible, which brings the viewer back to a heightened physical presence."

47105.de:
The photo comes from Cloe Jancis and Sigrid Viir's exhibition "On some more energetic days you put on your mask too firmly in front of the mirror, so that it bites into your skin". The impulse for the birth of the exhibition was the project "Isolation Dialogues" initiated by the Photography Museum in spring 2020, the aim of which was to document the sense of the isolation period and the newly arisen situation. The title of the exhibition comes from a short essay by Maris Karjatse.
The artists' visual dialogue proceeded by interpreting, mixing and further developing each other's ideas. 47424.d: Muravskaja kes tavaliselt reageerib teravalt ühiskondlikele probleemidele, pöördub seekord vee ja valguse läbi nähtud poeetiliste abstraktsete kujutluspiltide poole. Ise on ta oma tööde kohta öelnud: „Oma töödega kutsun ka vaatajat aeglustama ja häälestama pilku ümber – astuma kõrvale lõputust uudiste- ja pildivoost, et taastada tundlikkus valguse ja aja suhtes ning märgata, kuidas kujutis sünnib siin ja praegu. See on rännak nähtava ja nähtamatu piirile, mis toob vaataja tagasi teravdatud füüsilisse kohalolusse.“
47424.de: Muravskaja, who usually reacts sharply to social problems, turns this time to poetic abstract imagery seen through water and light. She has said of her works: "With my works I also invite the viewer to slow down and re-tune their gaze – to step aside from the endless stream of news and images, in order to restore sensitivity to light and time, and to notice how the image is born here and now. It is a journey to the border between the visible and the invisible, which brings the viewer back to a heightened physical presence."

47452.d: Teos kujutab endast tervet rida savist modelleeritud päid, mille loomiseks on kunstnik saanud impulsi Tartu Jaani kiriku skulptuuridest. Edith Karlson loob oma portreede galerii tuttavate abiga. Kõik nad töötasid kunstniku ateljees, enamus neist ei olnud mitte kunagi varem savi puutunud. Kunstnikul oli ambitsiooni paluda portreteerida teda ennast. Ometi paneb iga autor oma töösse suure osa iseendast, luues ka enda kohalolu portreede galeriis.  Kunstnik eksponeerib portreesid nii, et need saavad Jaani kiriku teostega samaväärse igavikulise tähenduse.
47452.de: The work consists of a whole row of heads modelled in clay, the impulse for whose creation the artist received from the sculptures of St. John's Church in Tartu. Edith Karlson creates her gallery of portraits with the help of acquaintances. They all worked in the artist's studio, most of them having never touched clay before. The artist had the ambition to ask that she herself be portrayed. Yet each author puts a great part of themselves into their work, thereby also creating their own presence in the gallery of portraits. The artist exhibits the portraits in such a way that they attain a significance as timeless as the works of St. John's Church.

65850.d:
Anna Mari Liivrand on skulptor ja installatsioonikunstnik, kelle loomingusse kuulub ka joonistusi. Oma õrna ja poeetilise visuaalse keele kaudu viitab Liivrand haprusele, kaduvusele ning sellega seotud melanhooliale tänapäeva ühiskonnas. Liivranna loomingus kerkib esile huvi igapäevaste objektide ja materjalide vastu, mis leiduvad meie kaasaegses elukeskkonnas. Viimastel aastatel on ta oma loomingus keskendunud ornamentidele ja nende ajaloole.
Liivranna kunstimeediumite, materjalide ja tehnikate käsitus on silmapaistvalt hübriidne: kunstnik arendab samu kujundeid skulptuuris ja joonistuses, kus kohati üsna heterogeensed koostisosad on allutatud ühe tervikliku narratiivi loomisele. Seejuures
65850.de:
Anna Mari Liivrand is a sculptor and installation artist whose oeuvre also includes drawings. Through her delicate and poetic visual language, Liivrand alludes to fragility, transience and the melancholy associated with them in contemporary society. Liivrand's work reveals an interest in everyday objects and materials found in our contemporary living environment. In recent years she has focused in her work on ornaments and their history.
Liivrand's approach to art media, materials and techniques is remarkably hybrid: the artist develops the same imagery in sculpture and drawing, where at times quite heterogeneous components are subordinated to the creation of a single coherent narrative. In doing so

65904.d: Jaanus Samma queer-temaatikat rahvakunsti esteetika kaudu käsitlev komplekt ühendab pärandi ja tänapäeval sotsiaalselt aktuaalsed küsimused vaimukaks kunstniku-uurimuseks, mille väljund laiendab (graafika)kunsti piire, jäädes samas tähelepanuväärselt visuaalse argumentatsiooni juurde.
65904.de: Jaanus Samma's set, addressing queer themes through the aesthetics of folk art, combines heritage and socially topical contemporary issues into a witty artist's investigation, whose output expands the boundaries of (graphic) art while remaining notably true to visual argumentation.

65954.d: Viktor Timofeevi joonistus on tänu autori Läti taustale laiendamas Eesti Kunstimuuseumi graafikakogu väikest Balti alakollektsiooni. Rahvusvaheliselt tunnustatud kunstniku teos on ilmekaks näiteks traditsioonilise joonistustehnika asjatundlikust kasutamisest kaasaegsete, mitmetähenduslikult avatud kujundite loomisel, genereerides uut tüüpi abstraktsuse autorit ümbritsevate argivaadete kummastuse kaudu (antud juhul on lähtepunktiks saanud vaade kunstniku vannitoa aknale ja selle peegeldusele seinal)
65954.de: Viktor Timofejev's drawing, thanks to the author's Latvian background, is expanding the small Baltic sub-collection of the graphic art collection of the Art Museum of Estonia. The work of this internationally recognised artist is a vivid example of the skilful use of traditional drawing technique in creating contemporary, ambiguously open images, generating a new type of abstraction through the estrangement of everyday views surrounding the author (in this case the starting point has been a view of the artist's bathroom window and its reflection on the wall)

66203.d: Huvitav näide monotüüpia tehnika harvaesinevast kasutusest kaasaegse noore autori poolt: ühelt poolt seostub see varasemate näidetega Eesti Kunstimuuseumi kogus, teiselt aga toob sisse tänapäeva tunnetuse ja tehnoloogilised uuendused.
66203.de: An interesting example of the rare use of the monotype technique by a contemporary young author: on the one hand it relates to earlier examples in the Art Museum of Estonia's collection, on the other hand it brings in a contemporary sensibility and technological innovations.

78854.d: Kristina Norman and Bita Razavi, in close dialogue with curator Corina L. Apostol, will present “Orchidelirium. An Appetite for Abundance”, an exhibition encompassing installation, film, photography, archive and performance—connecting the past with the present, all through the lens of colonial botany and its socio-political ramifications. The artists and curator, with the guidance of advisor Sadiah Boonstra, and the contributions of a team of creative collaborators will create an immersive environment, featuring a film trilogy by Norman and a performative spatial intervention by Razavi. The exhibition takes as its point of departure the overlooked story of the Estonian nineteenth-century artist and world traveler Emilie Rosalie Saal. Her work as an artist of tropical botanical flora combined with her personal history serves as a case study for entangled histories of self-determination, colonial experiences, neo-colonial structures, botany, science and art. The title of the project reflects the orchid madness that gripped Europeans in the nineteenth century, Saal included, fed by an abundance of botanical illustrations that erased contexts and promoted an extractivist vision of loca

Presented at the church of Chiesa di Santa Maria delle Penitenti, the exhibition explored primitive human urges in their banality and solemnity and questions the possibility of redemption in a world that is never worthy of it. The exhibition was created in collaboration with dramaturge Eero Epner. Located in Cannaregio overlooking the district’s canal, the interior of the church, which dates back to the 18 th century, helped to build the emotional atmosphere of the exhibition. There, everything was left unchanged, even the dust of the centuries past remained. Karlson used the abandoned space as a metaphor for being human, equally sad, and incomplete. Full of cracks and fissures, through which eventually, perhaps, a redeeming light will shine. The exhibition spaces were filled with clay and concrete sculptures that evoke the inevitable misfortune of being born, and the always-endeavouring nature of being human. 78858.d: The Estonian Centre for Contemporary Art is proud to announce artist Merike Estna has been selected to represent Estonia at the 61st Venice Biennale. The 61st International Art Exhibition La Biennale di Venezia takes place in 2026. Merike Estna is a painter based in Tallinn and Mexico City. Her work focuses on the processes of painting as well as integrating works of art and life. Estna often uses craft practices, combining these with an expanded approach to painting to highlight traditions that have not been traditionally recognised in the medium of painting. The open call for the 2026 Estonian pavilion received 25 submissions. The selection process was conducted in two stages by an international jury. Regarding Merike Estna’s work, the jury was impressed by her ability to use the medium of painting as a space for politically and socially relevant questions, as well as the grounds for activating questions of artist labour. The jury recognised Estna’s work for its maturity and impact, appreciated the artist’s insistence on situating painting at the intersection of performance and the social.
